A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 18-page versions of the same IMSE paper, including Appendices A–H. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison reveal no material gaps; pages 3–18 are identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original IMSE and IMSE-Retrieval experiments, ablations and robustness analyses in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experimental results, including benchmark accuracies, component ablations and the recurring-domain evaluation in Appendix H.

M1.justification: The singular-value adaptation procedure, diversity maximization objective and domain-aware spectral code retrieval are identical. The introduction's wording correction does not change any method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-C/R/A, ImageNet-3DCC, OfficeHome and DomainNet. Single-domain, continual, gradual, non-i.i.d. and recurring-domain scenarios are all retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including TENT, SAR and DPAL in the MAE/CLIP and appendix benchmark comparisons, and TENT, CoTTA and ViDA in continual adaptation.

E3.justification: The 50,000-image single-domain and 5,000-image continual ImageNet-C protocols, severity schedules, normalization, model configurations and optimization settings are unchanged. Appendix H retains the same ten-round recurring-domain design.

E4.justification: Sections 5–6 and the appendices retain identical singular-value selection analyses, loss and module ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity tests, non-i.i.d. robustness tests, diversity analyses and domain-descriptor comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix H's ten sequential adaptation rounds are unchanged and are not independent repeated-run estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings are identical. For example, both report 69.0% supervised IMSE accuracy in Table 1, 64.4% CTTA accuracy in Table 4, and 65.1% average recurring-domain accuracy in Table 17.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the spectral-expert definitions, orthogonality reasoning, alignment statistics and KL-based retrieval formulation are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about parameter-efficient adaptation, preserving feature diversity, retrieving domain knowledge and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of feature collapse, complementary losses, detection thresholds and domain-bank behavior are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning singular-vector memory and domain-bank storage.

D1.justification: Appendix A's implementation details and hyperparameters, the hardware and computational-cost disclosures, the reproducibility statement and the code-access link are identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations and references are unchanged, including the positioning relative to existing TTA methods and singular-value fine-tuning approaches.

P1.justification: On page 2, 'To handle(or address) those limitations' becomes 'To address those limitations.' The arXiv version/date stamp also changes. All other prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–17 retain identical displays, captions and placement. The wording correction only rewraps text within the existing page 2 paragraph; the page arrangement is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 removes one drafting alternative from the introduction and updates the arXiv stamp. This provides slight editorial polish, but the scientific argument, evidence, reproducibility information, limitations and appendices are otherwise identical, yielding no meaningful overall quality change.
